title: Level 3 (Advanced) - D-11
notes:
West leads the ♥J against 3NT. South has 6 top tricks (2 hearts, given the lead, the ♦A, and 3 clubs). South can easily build 2 tricks in spades and the diamond suit could provide up to 4 extra winners. South's 4th club could also come into play.

South must time the play carefully in order to maximize his chances. After winning West's heart opening lead South should lay down the ♦A. This is a safety play against West being dealt a singleton ♦K. South will never require more than 4 diamond tricks for his contract so he can afford to make this play (versus a first round diamond finesse). If the ♦K drops then South can concede a diamond trick to the defense and he will have enough tricks for his contract.

When both defenders follow to the first round of diamonds, but the ♦K does not drop, South should play a club to the dummy and test that suit by playing 2 more rounds. If both defenders follow to 3 rounds of clubs, South's remaining club will be his 7th winner and South can knock out the ♠A to ensure 9 tricks.

If one of the defenders discards on the third round of clubs (or sooner), 2 spades tricks will not be enough for the contract. South will need a favorable diamond lie to get home and the lead is in the right hand to play that suit. The contract will succeed unless East discards, but the contract can never be made if West has 2 diamond stoppers and clubs are 4-2. The recommended line will lead to success whenever it is possible to make the contract.
